A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioProBench, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 ends after 11 pages and v3 after 12 pages, both with references and without the cited appendices. Missing material prevents checking relocated Bio-LLM comparisons and detailed implementation and validation evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations across protocol tasks, including numerical results in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds ProAgent results, external LAB-Bench evaluation, and a human-versus-LLM-judge validation.

M1.justification: v3 Section 4 introduces ProAgent, with task classification, retrieval using task-dependent chunk granularity, hybrid semantic/lexical search, and task-selected generator models. v1 discusses RAG as a possible application and future direction without implementing this system. Renaming the retained protocol collection BioProCorpus does not itself establish a corpus-construction method change.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates 108 protocol-related LAB-Bench questions as an external, out-of-distribution test population; v1 only discusses LAB-Bench as prior work. The six-source protocol collection and five core BioProBench tasks remain.

E2.justification: The same ten general-purpose models remain in the main comparisons. v1 also tabulates BioMedGPT-10B, BioMistral-7B, and BioMistral-7B-DARE, whereas v3 directs Bio-LLM results to missing Appendix G.6. Their exact participation cannot be checked, so relocation cannot reliably be classified as comparator removal or retention.

E3.justification: v3 adds RAG/no-RAG comparisons, evaluation on 108 external questions, and blinded human validation on 200 randomly sampled instances. It also reports a separate one-shot GEN prompting condition. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the common benchmark retains approximately 1,000 instances per task and its existing metrics. Detailed appendix protocols are unavailable.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained prompting comparisons, v3 newly reports ORD sequence-length and failure analyses, PQA numerical perturbations testing memorization, GEN one-shot prompting analysis, and SR/SP threshold and metric validation. Human validation of the reasoning judge is also added. These substantially broaden the questions examined, although detailed supporting plots and breakdowns reside in missing appendices.

E5.justification: Neither supplied main text specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v3 newly claims that SR/SP correlate significantly better with judgment, but the statistical procedures are deferred to missing Appendix F.3. Changes in statistical estimation and uncertainty reporting therefore cannot be assessed reliably.

E6.justification: v3 adds ProAgent outcomes, including 85.08% PQA accuracy and 81.9% ERR F1, external evaluation results, and 94.21% judge–human agreement. These are new experimental conditions, not improvements in the unchanged baseline systems. Most retained scores match, but GPT-4o direct-GEN SR changes from 37.85% in v1 Table 6 to 37.50% in v3 Figure 6. New reporting is internally inconsistent: ProAgent GEN SR is 62.24% in Section 5.2 but 63% in Figure 7.

T1.justification: The supplied formal content retains the keyword precision/recall/F1 definitions and the same SR/SP equations and 0.7 similarity threshold. v3 adds an empirical justification for the threshold, not a revised mathematical definition or proof. No new theorem, formal assumption, or derivation is presented.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on constructing a benchmark and diagnosing LLM weaknesses, with RAG left for future work. v3 makes ProAgent and demonstrated corpus-based performance improvement central contributions, including a state-of-the-art advancement claim in the abstract. This substantially expands the paper's claimed contribution beyond diagnosis.

C2.justification: v3 interprets retrieval gains as evidence for corpus utility, reduced hallucination, and transferability, and numerical-perturbation stability as evidence for contextual reasoning rather than memorization. It distinguishes beneficial one-shot guidance from disruptive zero-shot GEN reasoning and acknowledges that ProAgent still omits nearly 38% of required steps. The earlier text-only and LLM-artifact limitations remain in the Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v3 adds concrete task/prompt examples in Figure 3, explicitly documents expert review of every test instance, and changes the dataset access account from GreatCaptainNemo to BioProBench. v1's task-generation model names, generation caps, and explicit licensing/internal-use explanation are no longer stated in the main text; their retention in missing appendices cannot be checked. These documentation differences do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of ProBio and LabSafety-Bench and references for CoT prompting and medical LLMs, while dropping references including BioMistral and the DeepSeek-V3 technical report. The central procedural-knowledge research gap remains. The change from BioProt to BioPlanner refers to the same cited work, rather than an additional comparison method.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, construction descriptions, experimental discussion, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v3 consistently distinguishes corpus, dataset, and benchmark; consolidates task evaluations under Section 5.1; introduces separate agent sections; and moves limitations into an Impact Statement. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The PQA/ORD tables become combined bar charts in Figure 5, and the GEN table becomes paired heatmaps in Figure 6. v3 adds task examples, a ProAgent architecture diagram, and agent-result charts in Figures 3, 4, and 7. Figure 1 panels are rearranged, Figure 2 is revised, and table layouts change substantially.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, ProAgent and human judge validation provide useful evidence about corpus utility and evaluation credibility. However, important new reliability claims depend on unavailable appendix protocols and analyses, and relocated Bio-LLM comparisons cannot be inspected. New figure–text discrepancies, including ProAgent GEN SR of 62.24% versus 63%, further limit confidence in the expanded evidence. These benefits and evidential limitations prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
